title: Lag (2026:769) om skyldighet för livsmedelsbutiker och apotek att ta emot kontant betalning
key_claim: Swedish statute obliges retail grocery stores and pharmacies to accept cash payment for goods and services at physical points of sale with a staffed till, subject to security and cost-of-handling exemptions.
frame_summary: Argues that cash acceptance at points selling basic necessities is a duty the state may impose on private retailers, not a commercial choice, and writes the exemptions narrowly around staff security and store viability.
verbatim_quote: Livsmedelsbutiker inom detaljhandel och apotek är skyldiga att ta emot kontant betalning vid försäljning av varor och tjänster på fysiska försäljningsställen med bemannad kassa.

0,1 prisbasbelopp och högst 25 mynt.

title: Cash remains most widely accepted payment method in euro area
key_claim: 92% of euro-area companies with physical points of sale accept cash in 2026, up from 90% in 2024, while mobile-payment acceptance rose from 36% to 68% over the same period.
frame_summary: Argues that cash acceptance in the euro area has stopped falling and is holding as the widest-accepted method, positioning cash as a stable base layer under a fast-growing digital layer rather than a residual in terminal decline.
verbatim_quote: In 2026, 92% of companies selling goods and services in physical locations in the retail trade, restaurants and cafés, hotels, and arts, entertainment and recreation sectors reported that they accept cash. This compares with 90% in 2024, suggesting that cash acceptance has rebounded after the decline observed during and after the pandemic.
verbatim_list: Acceptance of card payments remained broadly stable at 88% between 2024 and 2026, while acceptance of mobile payments rose sharply from 36% to 68% of companies over the same period.
The survey covered 8,205 companies across all 21 euro area countries. Interviews were conducted between February and April 2026.
notes: Primary survey release. Carries both the confirmatory acceptance figure and the strongest counter-datum, that mobile acceptance is growing far faster than cash acceptance. title: Cash acceptance in the Netherlands remains stable
key_claim: 78% of Dutch retailers ask customers to pay in cash when card payments are not possible and 47% deliberately hold extra change so they can keep trading during a disruption.
frame_summary: Argues that cash acceptance in the Netherlands is holding up and that its main remaining job is as a fallback during electronic-payment outages, which is why DNB monitors acceptance annually and why a statutory acceptance duty is being prepared.
verbatim_quote: For example, 78% of retailers ask customers to pay in cash when card payments are not possible. In addition, 47% deliberately keep extra change on hand so that they can continue to operate in such situations.
verbatim_list: In addition, a legal obligation to accept cash payments up to €3,000 has been proposed,which should ensure that cash remains widely accepted by retailers and other service providers.
At 4% of the outlets visited , a sticker clearly marked ‘PIN only’ indicated that customers could only pay by card.
notes: Annual acceptance monitor. Supplies the operational-behaviour evidence that retailers already act as the contingency layer. title: An efficient and secure payment system in more turbulent times
date_evidence: Published 10 June 2026 09:00 (page also carries meta-article:published_time: 6/10/2026 9:00:00 AM)
key_claim: Norges Bank's Financial Infrastructure Report 2026 states that contingency arrangements will not be enhanced until the proposed preparedness measures are implemented, and that cash still plays an important role for contingency preparedness.
frame_summary: Argues that Norway's payment-preparedness gap is an implementation problem rather than a design problem, and that cash holds its contingency role precisely because the digital fallback measures are not yet in place.

title: Tuomas Välimäki: Central banks and the future of money - trust, resilience and renewal
key_claim: Cash in circulation relative to GDP has increased by more than 50% in the euro area, growing faster than deposits, even as the transaction share of cash in Finland fell to roughly one in ten in-store payments.
frame_summary: Argues that falling cash use does not mean falling demand for central bank money, and that payments should be treated as critical national infrastructure requiring deliberate redundancy rather than optimised purely for efficiency.
verbatim_quote: At the same time, cash in circulation relative to GDP has increased by more than 50% in the euro area, growing faster than deposits.
verbatim_list: Now, the share of cash is closer to one out of ten transactions.
What looks inefficient in normal times may be valuable redundancy in a crisis.
notes: Central-bank speech republished by the BIS. Analytical commentary by a named senior official, classified Tier 2 per the tier rubric edge case. title: Europe's money evolves so people's freedom to pay remains
key_claim: The ECB strongly supports the Single Currency Package proposal on the legal tender of cash, which would safeguard acceptance and availability and align cash policies across the euro area.
frame_summary: Argues that euro cash and the digital euro are one currency in two technologies and should be legislated together, so that acceptance duties for physical cash and legal-tender status for the digital euro are settled in the same instrument.
verbatim_quote: We strongly support the proposal on the legal tender of cash as it safeguards its acceptance and availability and finally aligns cash policies across the euro area.
verbatim_list: However, between 2021 and 2024 cash acceptance decreased from 96% to 88%.
notes: ECB Executive Board speech to the European Parliament ECON Committee. Establishes the EU legislative vehicle for the acceptance duty. title: Regulating Cash Distribution in Australia: Conclusions Paper
key_claim: The CFR and the ACCC published a Conclusions Paper setting out a regulatory framework for cash distribution, following a 2025 consultation that drew 47 submissions and around 1,200 emails from members of the public.
frame_summary: Argues that cash distribution has become a sector requiring purpose-built regulation rather than commercial contracting, because the cash-in-transit market has concentrated to the point where continuity can no longer be assumed.
verbatim_quote: have released a Conclusions Paper on a regulatory framework for cash distribution.
verbatim_list: The CFR and ACCC received 47 submissions, around 1,200 emails from members of the public, and met with a wide range of stakeholders bilaterally and as part of industry roundtables.
notes: Structural anchor. Canonical regulator statement of the Australian cash-distribution regime that the August 2026 legislation implements. title: Banks welcome passage of legislation to regulate Australia's cash-in-transit sector
key_claim: The Cash Distribution Framework Bill 2026 passed the Australian Parliament on 20 August 2026, against a background in which cash usage has fallen from 70 per cent of payments two decades ago to around 15 per cent, and banks and retailers have injected over $100 million above contractual conditions into Armaguard over two years.
frame_summary: Argues from the industry side that regulated cash distribution is a necessary safety net, while making the cost case that the declining transaction base cannot fund the network unaided, so pricing certainty and defined service standards are the industry's condition for continuing to carry it.
verbatim_quote: Given cash usage has fallen from 70 per cent two decades ago to around 15 per cent now, there are clear challenges and cost pressures when it comes to cash distribution.
verbatim_list: That's why banks and retailers have stepped-up, injecting over $100 million in financial assistance above contractual conditions to Armaguard over the past two years.

The ABA welcomes today's passage through the Parliament of the Cash Distribution Framework Bill 2026, an important safety net shoring up the ongoing distribution and availability of cash across the economy.
notes: Industry association, positional by construction. Used for the dated legislative event and for the counter-argument's cost and volume evidence, not as an analytical anchor.
